text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- State-owned bank Postipankki lowers savings account interest rate to one percent from two percent, effective from next February.
- The Gulf of Bothnia is becoming a new industrial cluster. Oulu is the second biggest high-tech center in Finland.
- Abortion pill has lowered the number of abortions in Finland but experts disagree whether it should become a non- prescription drug. @
- Statisics Finland study suggests that new wood product innovations could help the economy .
- A cut in the EU's grain support would decrease Finnish producers' income by 100 million markka.
- The average industry worker aged during the recession years 1990-1993.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Recycling of paper and cardboard packages is becoming increasingly effective -- the paper industry may get 100,000 tonnes of new recycled raw material in the next few years. @
DEMARI
- Justice Minister Kari Hakamies wants judges to be selected by tests and interviews.
- Labour Minister Liisa Jaakonsaari wants to tighten cooperation between the state and the municipalities in solving the unemployment problem.
- The military wants to speed up the purchase of new transport helicopters.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- The Green Party hopes to increase its local government seats to 500 in this autumn's polls. @
AAMULEHTI

- Following the EU's ruling on the Bosman case which reduced restrictions on foreign players in European leagues, the number of foreign ice-hockey players in the Finnish league due to start in two weeks will rise to 46.
KAUPPALEHTI
- State revenue from tobacco accise likely to fall 300 million markka short of a budgeted 3.3 billion this year.
